title: Pullback compatibility of the zero locus
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism, and let $M$ and $N$ be invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. For an $\mathcal O_X$-linear morphism $\varphi:M\to N$, one has $\varphi.zeroLocus.comap\,g=(g^*\varphi).zeroLocus$, where $g^*$ is the module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$. By [lem-pc-invertible-sheaf-instance] $M$ and $N$ satisfy the invertibility hypothesis of [lem-pc-invertible-common-free-generator]; applied at $x=g(y)$ with $W=X$, it gives an affine open $U\ni g(y)$ with free generators $e_M$ of $M$ and $e_N$ of $N$ over $U$. Since $e_N$ is a free generator, $\varphi(e_M)=b e_N$ for a unique $b\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$. Choose an affine open $V$ around $y$ inside the open $g^{-1}(U)$ (affine opens form a basis). Applying [lem-pc-zero-scheme-pullback-local-coefficient] to these generators produces free generators of $g^*M,g^*N$ on $V$ with coefficient $g.appLE\,U\,V\,b$.

The closed subscheme $\varphi.zeroLocus.comap\,g$ is by definition the one cut out by the ideal sheaf of the projection $\varphi.zeroLocus\times_XY\to Y$. By [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension] applied to the closed subscheme $\varphi.zeroLocus$, $g$, and the affine opens $U$, $V\subseteq g^{-1}(U)$, its ideal on $V$ is the ideal generated by the image under $g.appLE\,U\,V$ of the ideal of $\varphi.zeroLocus$ on $U$. By [lem-pc-zero-scheme-ideal-local] the latter is $\operatorname{Ideal.span}\{b\}$, so the extended ideal is $\operatorname{Ideal.span}\{g.appLE\,U\,V\,b\}$: an element of the extended ideal is a sum of products of images of elements of $(b)$, and each is divisible by the image of $b$; conversely the image of $b$ belongs to it. Apply [lem-pc-zero-scheme-ideal-local] again on $V$ to the generators and coefficient from step 1 (the pulled-back modules are invertible, being locally free of rank one with the free generators of [lem-pc-zero-scheme-pullback-local-coefficient] around every point). It gives exactly the same ideal for the zero locus of the pulled-back morphism.

The opens $V_y$ of steps 1-2 cover $Y$ because $y\in V_y$ for every $y$. For either ordering of the two ideal-sheaf data, the ideal inclusion holds on every $V_y$ by step 2; the affine-cover locality of ideal-sheaf inclusion therefore gives both global inclusions. Antisymmetry gives equality of their ideal-sheaf data and hence of the closed subschemes.
